articles.summary: First patients enrolled in multi-center trial evaluating MRD-guided escalation for patients with advanced melanoma Natera, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced the enrollment of the first patients in a new Signatera-guided trial in melanoma ( NCT07504796 ), sponsored by NYU Langone Health. The study uses Signatera to guide treatment escalation for patients with advanced or metastatic melanoma, an aggressive form of skin cancer. The current standard of care for these patients is combination immunotherapy until clinical progression. This trial is designed to identify patients who may need earlier intervention by detecting persistent molecular residual disease (MRD) prior to radiographic progression. articles.summary: Designation supports the development of a blood-based assay intended to screen for various cancers Natera, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced that its multi-cancer early detection (MCED) assay has been granted Breakthrough Device designation (BDD) by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The BDD is designed for novel technologies that enable more effective diagnosis or treatment of life-threatening or irreversibly debilitating diseases or conditions. Natera’s MCED assay analyzes cell-free DNA in the blood to screen for multiple cancers. In granting the BDD, the FDA assessed data from 12 cancer types and considered sensitivity, specificity, and cancer signal origin (CSO) performance. articles.summary: TransCode will use Signatera™ to identify MRD-positive patients eligible for enrollment Natera, Inc. (Nasdaq: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, and TransCode Therapeutics, Inc . (Nasdaq: RNAZ), a clinical stage company pioneering immuno-oncology and RNA-based therapeutics for the treatment of high-risk and advanced cancers, today announced a strategic collaboration in colorectal cancer (CRC). The collaboration will support enrollment for TransCode’s Phase 2a trial evaluating TTX-MC138 in patients with CRC. Patients will be eligible for enrollment if they have completed curative-intent therapy and remain positive for molecular residual disease (MRD), as detected by Natera’s Signatera test, with no radiographic evidence of disease. The collaboration aims to surface patient populations who meet the trial’s MRD-positive eligibility criteria more efficiently, streamline site-level identification, and optimize the pace and quality of enrollment for the study.
articles.title: Natera and TransCode Therapeutics to Collaborate on Phase 2a Trial of TTX-MC138 in Colorectal Cancer

articles.summary: Analyses drawn from a large real-world database of patients underscore how genetic testing can support better care in chronic kidney disease (CKD) Natera, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced new data that was recently presented at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026, highlighting the unique value genetic testing can provide for patients with CKD. These 18 abstracts, including three oral presentations, add to the growing support for Renasight, Natera’s genetic test for CKD. Among the key findings were data from a large, real-world database of patients with indicators of kidney disease. One such analysis revealed significant delays in diagnosing and managing CKD. Among patients with incident CKD, the median time from the first abnormal kidney indicator to a documented diagnosis was about 5.3 years, with median eGFR falling from 75 to 66 mL/min/1.73 m² in the two years before diagnosis.
